visuals.instructionalPurpose: Make observable forms concrete before reconstructing a cross.
visuals.introductionAnchor: Before following the experiment, look at the characteristics Mendel could compare.
visuals.viewingGuidance: Look at purple/white flowers, then round/wrinkled seeds. Keep the characteristic separate from its two forms. Read yellow-left/green-right seed pixels.
visuals.resultingExplanation: Phenotypes can be observed and compared; a picture alone does not reveal the genotype or the result of a cross.
visuals.caption: Six visible contrasts in pea plants. Compare the two forms within a characteristic; the picture does not show a cross or its offspring.
visuals.alt: Six pea-plant contrasts: long and short stems; purple and white flowers; round and wrinkled seeds; yellow and green seeds; green and yellow pods; inflated and pinched pods. The seed-colour drawing places yellow on the left and green on the right, although its caption lists green first.
sourceCautions: Image has six contrasts, not the seven in textbook Figure 17.4; flower position is absent.
Embedded seed-colour caption lists green first but pixels show yellow left, green right. Original image bytes are retained.

visuals.instructionalPurpose: Show the correct flower-colour experiment before any seed-shape representation or chromosome conclusion.
visuals.introductionAnchor: The whole sequence is visible in the table. Read it from top to bottom.
visuals.viewingGuidance: Follow P chosen purple/white true-breeding parents, F1 offspring grown to flowering, then F1 self-pollination and F2 purple/white observations. Read starting conditions before outcomes.
visuals.resultingExplanation: F1 differs from a blending prediction; F2 observations create the reappearance problem. This is an observation sequence, not a premature P/p calculation.
visuals.caption: The flower-colour experiment, one generation at a time
visuals.status: New text/table representation expressly permitted by the user; grounded in source, not an extracted picture and not a derived raster crop.

placement.heading: Take the same question from flower colour to seed shape

visuals.instructionalPurpose: Show the seed-shape observation sequence after an explicit transition from the flower experiment.
visuals.introductionAnchor: In this model, the shape being scored belongs to each offspring seed with its own genotype.
visuals.viewingGuidance: Read P, F1 and F2 from top to bottom. One drawn seed stands for a group/category, not a sample count. Arrows abbreviate reproduction; identify the missing egg/sperm step.
visuals.resultingExplanation: The seed-shape pattern shares the flower experiment’s explanatory problem. Fractions are model expectations; the source drawing’s F1 intercross differs in arrangement from the preceding flower self-pollination account.
visuals.caption: Round and wrinkled seed forms followed through P, F1 and F2. The fractions summarize the model's expected proportions; they do not promise exact counts in every cross.
visuals.alt: Seed-shape sequence with a round and a wrinkled P parent, an all-round F1 generation, and an F2 generation showing round and wrinkled seeds. The drawing labels the schematic F2 proportions three quarters round and one quarter wrinkled and describes crosses between F1 plants.
sourceCautions: This is seed shape, never flower colour.
Original text saying F1 offspring produced smooth peas can blur offspring seeds versus plants; adjacent learner prose distinguishes these generations.
The original 3:1-each-cross wording is not an exact-count guarantee.

placement.heading: Separate the pair, then separate the copies

visuals.instructionalPurpose: Distinguish homologue separation from later sister-chromatid separation using one deliberately selected pair.
visuals.introductionAnchor: Use the chromosome drawing to distinguish those two separations.
visuals.viewingGuidance: Follow only the long blue/red pair in the left-hand arrangement: two X-shaped copied homologues, one in each middle cell, then separated long rods at the bottom. Explain the Metaphase II label.
visuals.resultingExplanation: Homologues are apart after the first division while sisters remain joined; sisters separate in the second. Colours distinguish homologues, not dominance or labelled R/r alleles. Plant gamete formation requires later reproductive stages.
visuals.caption: Follow the long pair within the left-hand arrangement. The two-colour scheme distinguishes homologues; it does not identify a dominant or recessive allele. The comparison between arrangements belongs to two-trait inheritance.
visuals.alt: A meiosis schematic with two homologous chromosome pairs, distinguished by length, and two possible arrangements. In each arrangement, copied X-shaped homologues separate into two cells; sister chromatids later separate into single chromosome rods. For this lesson, follow only the long blue and long red chromosomes in the left-hand arrangement.
sourceCautions: Image shows two pairs and two arrangements. Second-pair assortment and the branch comparison are deferred to lesson05.
Image contains no R/r locus labels, no pre-copying stage and no complete pea reproductive life cycle. These limits are explicit in the teaching.
No full-identity claim about sister chromatids throughout all meiotic events is made. Image47, which includes crossover context, is not selected.

visuals.instructionalPurpose: Connect the known true-breeding parents to the inferred F1 genotype after gamete production has been taught.
visuals.introductionAnchor: Look first at the parent labels in this drawing.
visuals.viewingGuidance: Read two-letter RR and rr parent labels, then the single Rr offspring category; supply the omitted R and r gamete contributions and fertilisation step.
visuals.resultingExplanation: Known RR×rr parentage identifies Rr even though round phenotype alone would leave RR/Rr possible. The r allele remains present.
visuals.caption: The RR × rr starting cross produces the Rr F1 category in the stated model. One seed icon represents the shared result, not a single offspring.
visuals.alt: A true-breeding round parent labelled RR is crossed with a true-breeding wrinkled parent labelled rr. Arrows lead to a round F1 seed category labelled Rr and 100 percent of offspring. The drawing abbreviates the gamete and fertilisation steps.
sourceCautions: The one icon is a category, not one offspring or an exact sample size.
Same media bytes also occur on slide24, but they are selected once here at slide18’s worked position.

visuals.instructionalPurpose: Organize all four contribution pairs after gametes and their probabilities are derived.
visuals.introductionAnchor: In the square below, read the letters across the top as sperm contributions and the letters down the left as egg contributions.
visuals.viewingGuidance: Read every edge and cell: top sperm R/r, left egg R/r, then RR, Rr, Rr, rr. Distinguish single-allele edge gametes from paired-allele interior offspring.
visuals.resultingExplanation: Two routes lead to the same heterozygous genotype; rr is possible through two existing recessive contributions. Equal segregation plus random fertilisation justifies each one-quarter probability.
visuals.caption: Rr × Rr contribution pairs. Edges describe gametes; interior entries describe offspring. Each row and each column has probability one half under the stated model.
visuals.alt: A two-by-two Punnett square with R and r across the top and R and r down the left. The four interior entries are RR, Rr, Rr and rr. In the accompanying explanation, top entries are sperm contributions and left entries are egg contributions.
sourceCautions: This original grid has no maternal/paternal labels. Learner prose explicitly assigns the same top-sperm/left-egg convention as the current native worked table.
Slides21/22 image27 and textbook17.7 use the reverse parental orientation; they are read as sources but not displayed here.
Repeated cell positions are contribution categories, not a schedule for four offspring.

visuals.instructionalPurpose: Show why grouping by allele pair and grouping by expression produce different ratios from the same contribution pairs.
visuals.introductionAnchor: The same reasoning gives ¼ to each of the four positions.
visuals.viewingGuidance: Read genotype row before phenotype row; combine the two Rr routes, then combine RR and Rr for round; verify both totals are one.
visuals.resultingExplanation: Addition combines mutually exclusive categories. Complete dominance changes phenotype grouping, not the allele pair.
visuals.caption: Group the same contribution pairs in two different ways
